To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The 64Cu and the 67Cu can be produced in the reactor using enriched zinc target, 2) The enriched zinc targets can be used to produce the 64Cu and and 67Cu with the yields of 95 and 99% respectively, 3) The enriched zinc target can be used to separate the copper isotopes from zinc with the separation factor greater than 103.
we were able to successfully irradiate enriched zinc targets and produce 64Cu and/or 67Cu in a reactor setting.
the use of enriched zinc targets in conjunction with boron nitride sample holders and a high flux reactor can produce 64Cu and67Cu in reasonable quantities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reactor production route for 64Cu and/or 67Cu.
the production of 67Cu and 64Cu for medical research applications using enriched zinc targets, irradiation of the targets in the MITR-II reactor and subsequent chemical separations.
the development of a reactor-based method to produce 64Cu and/or 67Cu for medical research studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of enriched zinc as a target material for the production of the medical isotopes 67Cu and 64Cu is an effective and efficient method of producing these in demand isotopes.
the production of 64Zn and 67Zh using enriched zinc targets is possible and that the development work conducted has provided the necessary data for the design of a full-scale irradiation facility.
the initial development and trial irradiations conducted were very successful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reactor-based production of 64 and 67Cu is feasible and that the production of 64Zn and 67Znzn is possible using the enriched zinc targets and ion exchange separations.

the production of the medical isotopes 67Cu and 64Cu via the reactor-based fast neutron 67Zn (n,p)67Cu and 67 Zn (n,p)64Cu reactions using enriched 67Zn and 64Zn target material is a promising method for the production of these isotopes.
we have demonstrated the ability of a research reactor to produce 64Cu and that we have successfully separated the copper from the irradiated targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of 67Zn is a limiting factor in the production of 64Zn, and that the 67Zn can be separated by ion exchange chromatography with a 1% HNO3 elution.
the production of 64Zn and 67Zu is achievable using enriched zinc targets and a fast reactor neutron flux.
the reactor production method for 64Cu and/or 67Cu is feasible and could be scaled up to provide sufficient activity for clinical trials.
